cf.title: Add a berief general comment on BTScanInsertData's nextkey and backward

input.subject: Add a berief general comment on BTScanInsertData's nextkey and backward

verdict_reasoning: No objection survived at levels 1a, 1b or 2. The patches change comments only in nbtree.h and nbtsearch.c, and Peter Geoghegan called the first comment reasonable in message #2. The remaining risk is whether the v2-0001 wording is accurate, and the material does not show that text.

brief.title: Comment fixes for nbtree nextkey, backward and _bt_binsrch
brief.problem: The comment on BTScanInsertData no longer explains the nextkey and backward fields and only points to _bt_first. The author thinks commit c9c0589fda0e removed the old text when the backward scan optimization changed their meaning. Readers of the nbtree code are the audience.
brief.proposed_design: Patch 0002 adds a short comment in nbtree.h: nextkey sets how the scankey boundary is read, backward marks a backward scan, and _bt_first has the details. Patch 0001 rewrites the _bt_binsrch comments in nbtsearch.c to separate internal page behavior from leaf page behavior, after a reviewer's remark. The patches change comments only.
author_claims: A brief, general description of nextkey and backward in BTScanInsertData helps readers.
The _bt_binsrch comment and the end of _bt_first do not contradict each other, but naming the leaf page would make this clearer.
The follow-up patch makes the difference between internal and leaf page behavior in _bt_binsrch clearer.
brief.thread_state: Peter Geoghegan called the first comment reasonable and asked whether the _bt_binsrch internal page comments, which seem to contradict _bt_first, should also change. The author posted v2 with a follow-up patch in March 2026 and asked if it helps; nobody has replied since.
unclear: The material does not show the new _bt_binsrch comment text in v2-0001, so reviewers cannot see whether it uses Geoghegan's pivot tuple and downlink explanation.
Whether the author's suggested edit to the end-of-_bt_first comment is part of v2.
Whether v2-0002 changes the nbtree.h wording from the first version.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: New comments in nbtree.h and nbtsearch.c must stay accurate when _bt_first or _bt_binsrch change.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: Does the new _bt_binsrch comment in v2-0001 use the pivot tuple and downlink explanation from message #2, or a different one?
Is the suggested edit to the comment at the end of _bt_first, from message #3, part of v2?
Does v2-0002 change the nbtree.h wording from the first version?

committability.owner_note: Peter Geoghegan replied in message #2 and asked for the _bt_binsrch change; a committer who knows nbtree search must confirm the v2-0001 wording.
committability.liability: The committer signs for the accuracy of two comments on nbtree search. A wrong comment misleads later readers, but no behavior changes.
committability.author_follow_up: The author posted v2 after the review and moved the entry through three CommitFests, most recently on 2026-10-23.

priority.reason: Two small comment-only patches help readers of the nbtree code and add no runtime cost. The entry has waited since March 2026 for a reply to v2 from someone who knows nbtree.

provisional_note: The new comment text in v2-0001 and v2-0002 was not read, so its accuracy against _bt_binsrch and _bt_first could not be checked.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: Using indexUnchanged with nbtree
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes nbtree skip the uniqueness check in _bt_check_unique() when the executor passes the indexUnchanged hint, so non-HOT UPDATEs on tables with unique B-tree indexes do less work. The author argued the skipped check only revisits the old row version that the UPDATE has just modified.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Peter Geoghegan pointed out that _bt_check_unique() sets LP_DEAD bits that kill_prior_tuple does not set for non-HOT updates fed by a scan of the same index, so skipping it loses that cleanup. He also said the patch turns indexUnchanged from a hint into a flag that must never be falsely set, and asked for a benchmark that shows a user benefit to justify that risk. The author ran out of time and the entry stalled from July, so Jaime Casanova marked it Returned with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
It is currently just supposed to be a hint, but your proposal
makes it truly critical.

precedents_retrieved.title: walsender.c fileheader comment
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch rewords the walsender.c file header comment on shutdown. It says that during logical replication the walsender switches to a "stopping" state, rejects further replication commands, processes existing WAL and then exits.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tomas Vondra pointed out that the comment's "stopping" state means WalSnd->state set to WALSNDSTATE_STOPPING, not the got_STOPPING flag. A walsender doing regular logical replication never enters that state, so the new wording was wrong. The author agreed and withdrew the patch, saying that someone who knows the difference better should clarify the comment.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: So from this point of view, the suggestion is actually wrong.

precedents_retrieved.title: Iterating on IndexTuple attributes and nbtree page-level dynamic prefix truncation
precedents_retrieved.summary: Patch 0001 adds an API to iterate over index tuple attributes and reuse the offset of the last extracted attribute, so extracting all attributes costs O(n) instead of O(n*n) when attcacheoff cannot be used. Patch 0002 uses this to truncate attribute prefixes dynamically during nbtree binary search within a page, as a first step toward prefix truncation in nbtree.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author's own June 2021 benchmarks showed regressions in multi-column indexes that can use attcacheoff: about 2% for insert and 15% for reindex with both patches. The author said this had to be fixed before commit, but no fixed version appears in the thread. In December 2021 Daniel Gustafsson moved the entry forward and noted that the patch no longer applied and needed a rebase. The visible messages do not show a rebased version or the final decision.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Evidently, this needs improvements in the (likely common) attcacheoff-enabled multi-column case; as I don't think we can reasonably commit a 10+% regression.

precedents_retrieved.title: Support to COMMENT ON DATABASE CURRENT_DATABASE
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes CURRENT_DATABASE a keyword that can stand for the current database name in COMMENT ON DATABASE, ALTER DATABASE (OWNER, SET, RESET) and SECURITY LABEL ON DATABASE. It aims to let a dump load into a differently named database; the pg_dump part was to come in a separate patch.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages show only the October 2017 close as Returned with Feedback, not the final rejection in March 2018. In that close, Daniel Gustafsson cited Nathan Bossart's review and the lack of a new version. That review found whitespace errors, a failing 'dbname' regression test, missing documentation, and repeated code that should become get_dbspec_name()/get_dbspec_oid() helpers. It also found inconsistent naming between DBSpecName and _equalDatabaseSpec().
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Based on this review, and that there hasn’t been a new version submitted, I’m marking this patch Returned with Feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: Use tuple-level SIREAD locks for index-only scans
precedents_retrieved.summary: Index-only scans that skip the heap would take tuple-level SIREAD locks instead of locking the whole heap page, with a fix to the outdated comment in nodeIndexonlyscan.c. A later experimental patch also skipped the btree page lock when the scan uses equality quals on all key columns of a unique index.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The patch stopped applying after a collision in the test files, and Daniel Gustafsson asked for a rebased version. No new version appears in the visible messages, so the entry was returned with feedback. Earlier, David Rowley found that deferrable unique constraints broke the btree lock skip, and Thomas Munro fixed that case in v4. Thomas Munro was still unsure the fix covered every case.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: This patch now fails to apply, probably due to a mostly trivial collision with fdd88571454e2b00dbe446e8609c6e4294ca89ae in the test files.

precedents_retrieved.title: Remove extra Sort node above a btree-compatible Index Scan
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch changes the planner's pathkey comparison so that an index from a B-tree-compatible access method in a different operator family is treated as matching the ORDER BY. This removes the extra Sort node above such an index scan, as seen with the xtree test module from the Index AM API cleanup series.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane objected that the patch ignores the operator family when deciding whether two pathkeys represent the same ordering, as in create_mergejoin_plan(). He said pathkeys are designed so that pointer comparison of canonical pathkeys is enough, and that the patch may cover up a break in that design. The author answered with context, and no revised patch appears in the visible messages.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
You can't just ignore the opfamily
etc. while deciding whether two pathkeys represent the same sort
ordering, as you did in create_mergejoin_plan().

precedents_retrieved.title: enum support in btree_gin and btree_gist
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds enum support to the btree_gin and btree_gist extensions, without distance operators and so without KNN support. The enum comparison goes through enum_cmp_internal, which uses the type cache for enums whose values are not in OID order.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Testing showed that GiST comparisons gave wrong results after alter type ... add value, because enum_cmp_internal expects fcinfo->flinfo and DirectFunctionCallN passes NULL. Tom Lane judged a NULL check too slow and said the proper fix is to pass the FunctionCallInfo through the btree_gist/gin intermediate layer, which touches almost every function. The author agreed but had no time to do this before the end of the commitfest.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
The problem is that the intermediate layer in btree_gist (and
probably btree_gin too, didn't look) does not pass through the
FunctionCallInfo data structure that's provided by the GIST AM.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert the GinMaxItemSize calculation so that we fit 3 tuples per page.
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert the GinMaxItemSize calculation so that we fit 3 tuples per page.
Reverted commit(s): Compress GIN posting lists, for smaller index size.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
Commit 36a35c55 changed the divisor from 3 to 6, for no apparent reason.
Reducing GinMaxItemSize like that created a dump/reload hazard: loading a
9.3 database to 9.4 might fail with "index row size XXX exceeds maximum 1352
for index ..." error. Revert the change.

While we're at it, make the calculation slightly more accurate. It used to
divide the available space on page by three, then subtract
sizeof(ItemIdData), and finally round down. That's not totally accurate; the
item pointers for the three items are packed tight right after the page
header, but there is alignment padding after the item pointers. Change the
calculation to reflect that, like BTMaxItemSize does. I tested this with
different block sizes on systems with 4- and 8-byte alignment, and the value
after the final MAXALIGN_DOWN was the same with both methods on all
configurations. So this does not make any difference currently, but let's be
tidy.

Also add a comment explaining what the macro does.

This fixes bug #12292 reported by Robert Thaler. Backpatch to 9.4, where the
bug was introduced.

roaster_notes.note: No precedent found: [P5] and [P3] are comment-only patches in other subsystems, and neither recorded reason (a wrong walsender state; no author reply to review) applies here. The thread cites no earlier attempt beyond commit c9c0589fda0e (message #1), which removed the old text and is not a rejected proposal.

The patches change only source comments in nbtree.h and nbtsearch.c. Nothing changes in SQL syntax, GUCs, pg_dump output, psql or what clients see, so the standards and compatibility angle has nothing to object to. Whether the new _bt_binsrch wording is accurate is a separate question, and the material does not show that text.

The patches change comments only, in nbtree.h and nbtsearch.c. They change no on-disk format, WAL record, catalog, wire protocol or struct layout, so this angle has nothing to object to. The nbtree VACUUM bookkeeping invariant does not apply because no VACUUM behavior changes.
The patches change only comments in nbtree.h and nbtsearch.c. They add no privilege, exposure, authentication or resource-use aspect, so the security angle has nothing to object to.

The patches change comments only, so non-users pay no runtime, ABI or upgrade cost, and the nbtree VACUUM bookkeeping invariant does not apply. Peter Geoghegan, who knows this area, called the first comment reasonable in message #2, and v2-0001 answers his own request; the v2-0001 wording is not in the material, so its accuracy could not be checked.

The patches change comments only, so no existing feature, extension or tool can meet this need. The existing pointer to _bt_first is the current way to learn what the fields mean, and the proposal only adds a short summary next to it, which is not a second mechanism.

The patch changes comments only, so the demand test does not apply in the usual way. It adds no user surface and puts no cost on non-users. The readers are nbtree code readers, and Peter Geoghegan called the first comment reasonable in message #2. Whether the v2 wording is correct is a separate question for other angles.
